# V1.7.4 — the web-app track

Opened 2026-08-03, successor to [v1.7.3.md](v1.7.3.md).

**Why this doc exists:** the web-app track ([web-phase-0-prep.md](../web/web-phase-0-prep.md)'s W-series) is now the next major body of work after receipt OCR, and it is a different concern from the native feature batch. Splitting it out lets **v1.7.3 cut as a receipt-OCR-only release** the moment its de-risking corpus lands, without the web work holding it open — the same reasoning that made v1.7.2 a single-item batch. The cross-platform-contract freeze moved here **unchanged** from [v1.7.3 Item 1](v1.7.3.md) (it keeps Item 1 here too); its 2026-08-03 grill outcome moved with it. Nothing about the item's design changed in the move.

**Booking convention for this doc:** native/Supabase execution of a W-series item gets booked here as a numbered Item, exactly like any other version doc. The W entry in [web-phase-0-prep.md](../web/web-phase-0-prep.md) stays the design home (the ask, the tensions, the grill outcome); this doc is the build ledger. Expect W3/W4/W7/W8/W9/W10 to land here as they are grilled and scheduled.

---

## Item 1 — Freeze the cross-platform contract (from Web Phase 0 W2)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE 2026-08-05** — [cross-platform-contract.md](../web/cross-platform-contract.md) is frozen §1–§9 with its Conformance checklist fully ticked, and the load-bearing deliverable shipped: [`CrossPlatformContractConformanceTest`](../../app/src/test/java/com/iponlove/app/core/util/CrossPlatformContractConformanceTest.kt), 15 JVM tests (suite 1328 green, `testStagingDebugUnitTest`). Doc-only plus one new test file — **no schema change, no Room change (stays v31), no production-code change**. The one sanctioned `⬜` is §7.5's allowed web origin, deferred to the hosting choice per the grill's definition-of-done amendment. See **Outcome** below. Previously: PLANNED, ✅ **GRILLED 2026-08-03** — booked 2026-07-29 (originally as v1.7.2 Item 2, then v1.7.3 Item 1; moved here 2026-08-03 when the web track was split into its own doc), grilled 2026-08-03, **not yet built**. The grill settled the two questions that needed a judgment call and produced [ADR-0063](../adr/0063-web-v1-is-online-only.md); see **Grill outcome** below, which supersedes the open questions listed further down. **Model: Opus, high effort** — it spans ~a dozen ADRs (0001/0002/0003/0005/0006/0007/0008/0009/0013/0043/0044/0053/0055) plus sync, money math and entitlement, and freezing a value here makes any client that drifts (**including Android**) the bug. **Primary deliverable is a doc, not a feature** — filling + freezing [cross-platform-contract.md](../web/cross-platform-contract.md), which today is a 9-section skeleton with 8 sections still `⬜ not frozen`. Expect a **secondary native code deliverable** (conformance tests + pinning currently-implicit values), so **no schema change and no Room change** (stays **v31**).
- **Request:** the native/repo execution of [web-phase-0-prep.md W2](../web/web-phase-0-prep.md#w2--freeze-the-cross-platform-contract-determinism--sync-protocol--money-math), the second of the two items that doc calls "highest leverage, both block real risk" — W1 was the first and shipped as [v1.7.2 Item 1](v1.7.2.md#item-1--lock-the-entitlement-columns-rls--validating-write-rpc-from-web-phase-0-w1). Every rule in the contract fails **silently** when a second client violates it: no crash, just duplicated rows or centavo-divergent numbers weeks later.
- **✅ Grill outcome (2026-08-03)** — supersedes "the sequencing tension" and "what the grill must resolve" bullets below, which are kept as the record of what the grill was asked to settle:
  1. **Question zero — proceed now, do not wait for W10.** The wait was circular (this item waited on W10, W10's entry says start it when the web build begins, the web build needs this contract), and the captain confirmed the web track is next up after receipt OCR and could begin within 48 hours. **Sequencing that dissolves the time pressure:** this item does not have to finish before the web track starts — W10 phase 1 (empty shared module + Kotlin/JS target, zero behavior change) can run in parallel. The hard requirement is only that the conformance vectors exist and pass **before W10 phase 2**, which is where the logic actually moves.
  2. **Scope correction — the conformance vectors are the load-bearing deliverable, not the prose.** Reason: `DeterministicUuid` is **not** `commonMain`-ready, contradicting W8's claim. It is Android-free but JVM-bound (`java.nio.ByteBuffer`, `java.security.MessageDigest`, `java.util.UUID`), so the extraction **rewrites** it onto different SHA-1 and UUID primitives rather than moving it — and a byte-order slip in that rewrite silently produces different ids, i.e. duplicate rows instead of merged ones. The vectors are the only mechanism that catches it. *(W8 and W10 corrected 2026-08-03; see **Follow-up to book** below.)*
  3. **§9 decided — leave grouped multi-row settlement Android-only; do not build the `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC now.** The question depended on an upstream one the grill also settled: **web v1 is online-only** ([ADR-0063](../adr/0063-web-v1-is-online-only.md)), so web has no local store to mirror Android's transaction with. Accepted because the gap is convenience, not correctness — per ADR-0055 the money end-state is identical however a lump is spread across same-direction debts. The **binding output is the forward-looking rule** now frozen in contract §9: any future all-or-nothing-across-tables feature is designed as a server-side RPC from the start if web needs to author it. **No ADR was needed for §9 itself** (as this item predicted, since the RPC is not being built); ADR-0063 covers the upstream online-only decision instead.
  4. **Definition-of-done amendment (see Verify below):** §7's allowed-web-origin line stays deliberately unfrozen pending the hosting choice.
- **Follow-up to book (found during the grill, not fixed here):** W8's "already written in `commonMain`-compatible style" claim listed `DeterministicUuid` incorrectly. The doc claims are corrected as of 2026-08-03, but the **extraction estimate** still needs revisiting — that file is a primitive swap plus its 6 call sites, not a move, and it is the highest-stakes file in the migration. Book against W10 when it is scheduled. Treat "zero Android imports" as necessary but **not sufficient** evidence of portability; each candidate file needs a JVM-only-type audit.
- **The sequencing tension to settle first (grill question zero — ANSWERED, see Grill outcome above):** W2's own status note says to grill it *"once W10 clarifies exactly which pieces move"* into the shared KMP module — under the 2026-07-28 architecture direction, §1/§1b/§2/§3/§4/§5/§6 become compiler-enforced-identical by construction rather than hand-followed, while §7 (image compression) and §9 (atomic writes) stay genuinely platform-specific. **My read, to be confirmed or overturned at the grill:** proceed anyway — W10 changes *who consumes* the frozen values (a spec a human follows vs. a spec the extraction is audited against), not *what the values are*, and the pinning work is the extraction's own acceptance criteria. W10 remains unbooked and unscheduled; blocking on it means the contract stays unfrozen through the whole pre-extraction window.
- **What the grill must resolve** (each maps to a `⬜` section + its "To pin at grill" bullet in [cross-platform-contract.md](../web/cross-platform-contract.md) — do not restate the skeleton here, fill it there):
  1. **§1 Deterministic UUIDs** — confirm the `{occurrenceDate}` string format is ISO `yyyy-MM-dd`; enumerate the full starter `{key}` list from `StarterCatalog`; pin namespace byte-order; produce **conformance vectors** (known name → expected UUID). Source: [DeterministicUuid.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/util/DeterministicUuid.kt) + its 6 call sites. §1b (notification composite ids) is **already ✅ live** and needs adoption, not grilling.
  2. **§2 LWW** — exact monotonic-bump semantics, clock-offset acquisition + refresh cadence, and the non-Android equivalent of `ClockOffsetStore`. ADR-0001/0002.
  3. **§3 FK order** — the single authoritative *full* ordering across every table now in `SyncTable` (the ADR-0009 nine, plus `savings_goals`/`goal_contributions`/`transaction_images`/`partner_debts`/`partner_debt_payments`, with `notifications` confirmed last), plus the per-table `server_rev > cursor` rule. **Note (2026-07-29):** [the subcategories item](deferred.md#item-4--subcategories-parentchild-category-hierarchy)'s grill briefly added an **intra-table** clause here — `categories` rows pushing parents-before-children, since [ADR-0061](../adr/0061-subcategories-two-level-owner-matched.md) would give `categories.parent_id` a self-referencing FK that table-level ordering cannot express. **That item was deferred the same day, so this clause is NOT part of the freeze** — §3 stays table-level-only. Re-add it if and only if it is un-deferred; it is recorded in ADR-0061 decision 7 so it can't be lost.
  4. **§4 Money math** — rounding mode + scale **per derived site** (balance ADR-0007, analysis aggregations, budget %, transfer split, debt netting, and `DebtAllocationCalculator.allocate` from ADR-0055), with worked examples as vectors.
  5. **§5 Conflict resolution** — the exact note conflict-copy algorithm (ADR-0003), the precise partner-row purge triggers (ADR-0005/0011), and the couple-RPC signatures + error shapes (ADR-0006/0008/0013).
  6. **§6 Seeding** — the server-side "already onboarded?" predicate and the tombstone-respect rule (absorbs W5).
  7. **§7 Images** — bucket/path naming, compression params, authenticated-URL scheme, storage RLS/CORS (absorbs W6, ADR-0043). Stays platform-specific under W10.
  8. **§8 Entitlement** — now answerable: fold in the **shipped** ADR-0060 RPC contract from v1.7.2 Item 1, including the correction that the lock is an **allowlist grant** (a new `users` column needs a matching `grant`) and that the RPC is a **passthrough with receipt validation deferred**. Cross-link ADR-0044 + [subscription-paywall-design.md](subscription-paywall-design.md); do not restate.
  9. **§9 Atomic multi-row writes** — the one genuine *architecture* decision in the batch, not a data-format one: leave grouped settlement Android-only, or build the `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC now so both clients can author it. ADR-0055. **(ANSWERED — see Grill outcome 3.)**
- **Change (provisional, to be replaced by the grill's output):**
  - Fill and mark ✅ FROZEN each section of [cross-platform-contract.md](../web/cross-platform-contract.md), ticking its Conformance checklist; flip W2's status in [web-phase-0-prep.md](../web/web-phase-0-prep.md).
  - Likely native code: a **conformance-vector test suite** in `app/src/test/` asserting the frozen UUID vectors and per-site money rounding — the mechanism that makes "Android drifted" a red build rather than a silent divergence. Any site where the contract's stated rounding turns out **not** to match the code becomes its own booked fix item, not a quiet edit inside this one.
  - Probable new ADR(s) only for §9 (and only if it decides to build the RPC); the other eight sections are *recording* existing decisions, so they belong in the contract doc, not in new ADRs.
- **✅ Outcome (2026-08-05):**
  - **§1** — namespace byte-order pinned as *most-significant-byte-first, then the UTF-8 name with no separator*; `{occurrenceDate}` confirmed ISO `yyyy-MM-dd` (it is `LocalDate.toString()`); the starter `{key}` catalog enumerated (14 categories + 3 accounts, frozen permanently — a rename forks every synced row); **23 name→UUID vectors** produced, including an empty-name vector that isolates the namespace serialization so a port debugs step 1 before anything else. A separate test hashes the same 16 bytes reversed and asserts a *different* id, so a byte-order-wrong port cannot accidentally pass.
  - **§2** — `stamp()` semantics pinned to the millisecond, including the tie-break (`floor` wins only if *strictly* after) and the fact that the +1ms floor is per-row and only applied where the caller passes the previous value. Offset comes from the `get_server_time()` RPC, recalibrated after every **full** sync only (not the debounced micro-syncs), persisted, defaulting to 0. **Round-trip latency is knowingly uncompensated** — recorded as accepted, not as a bug to fix.
  - **§3** — the authoritative ordering is the **23-entry `SyncTable` enum**, which turned out to differ from ADR-0009's nine-table list in shape, not just length (`transaction_images` before `budgets`; the debt tables before `notes`; the partner views as one contiguous trailing block). Also frozen: **pull is parallel**, so §3.1 is a *push* guarantee.
  - **§4** — a per-site scale/rounding table covering all 19 derived sites, with the two easiest-to-mis-port ones called out explicitly (budget percent **truncates** after a scale-4 divide, so 79.99% reads 79; projection is `avg × buckets`, not `total × ratio`), plus **16 worked vectors**. Added a clause the skeleton didn't anticipate: **timezone is part of money math** — monthly aggregates key on the PH-local calendar, so a browser in another zone would sort a month-boundary expense differently with no row-level conflict to detect.
  - **§5** — the note conflict-copy algorithm written out as 9 exact steps (fresh v4 id, `"[Conflict Copy] "` prefix, forced private, `pending_sync = true`); the eight partner purge predicates tabulated; the unpair purge pinned to the **set→null transition** on the user's own `couple_id` with its two guards and the eight cursor resets; all eight RPCs given signatures, return types and **verbatim** error strings (they surface as HTTP 400 / `P0001`, and there are no distinct SQLSTATEs to match on).
  - **§6** — the guard is a four-clause predicate, and the nuance that matters for web is that on Android it reads *server* state **through Room after a successful sync**. Web has no local store, so it must issue the count against Supabase directly. Ruling: **web may seed, and must run the guard** (rejected: "web never seeds").
  - **§7** — frozen from the Android sources; confirmed **no new storage policy is needed**. Added an orphan rule web needs and Android doesn't: upload first, write the row second, best-effort delete on row-write failure.
  - **§8** — folded in the shipped ADR-0060 contract, including the correction that the lock is an **allowlist grant** (a column-level revoke is a silent no-op against a table-level grant) and its standing cost: adding a `users` column is now a two-step change whose failure mode is a field that quietly stops syncing. The RPC's six frozen behaviours are written out, and §8.4 states plainly that it is an **unvalidated passthrough** so no future reader mistakes §8 for "entitlement is secured."
  - **§9** — already frozen by the grill; carried over unchanged.
  - **No behavioural discrepancy found**, so nothing needed booking as a follow-up fix. Three *documentation* drifts were found and corrected in the contract (which is now authoritative): ADR-0009's stale ordering, the parallel-pull deviation, and the "server check" wording in §6. They are listed at the foot of the contract doc.
- **Explicitly NOT in this item:** building the KMP `shared` module (W10), any web-app code (W8), the web purchase path (W7), and Play receipt validation (still deferred from v1.7.2 Item 1). Changing Android behavior to match a newly-written contract value is also out — discrepancies get booked, not fixed inline.
- **Verify:** build green + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green with the new conformance tests. **Tier-1 tests required** — this is squarely sync/money/mapper territory. No on-device check needed for the doc work itself; if any Android code changes to satisfy a vector, that change gets its own on-device script per the usual rule. The real acceptance test is that every Conformance-checklist box is ticked and no section is left `⬜` — **amended 2026-08-03 by the grill:** with exactly one sanctioned exception, the specific web origin admitted by §7's storage RLS/CORS, which cannot be pinned until hosting is chosen (Vercel vs. Cloudflare Pages, open in [W8](../web/web-phase-0-prep.md#w8--web-app-greenfield-foundational-design)). Record that line as explicitly pending rather than inventing a value. §9 is already frozen by the grill, so the fill pass covers §1–§8.
